title: BlueHarbor - inference stack assessment / exit planning
summary: Initial discovery to understand BlueHarbor's plan to move off a mixed OpenAI + self-hosted vLLM/TGI stack. Key concerns: latency parity, eval/regression testing, data residency, and total cost of ownership for Dedicated vs Private. Action: send pricing, security pack, and a runbook for parity benchmarks; schedule a POC run for January.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-12-08
- Start: 14:00 PT
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: James (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Aisha (CTO), Tom (Lead ML), Dana (Cloud Infra), Maggie (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): blue harbor evaluating moving away from OpenAI + in-house vLLM/TGI. Looking for predictable latency for product features and enterprise controls. Action items for Redwood to follow up with pricing + security docs + benchmark plan.

00:00 Speaker 1 (James): Hey everyone thanks for joining, um, this is James from Redwood Inference. Couple people on my side, Priya and Marco, say hi.
00:07 Speaker 2 (Priya): Hi all.
00:09 Speaker 3 (Marco): Hey team, excited to dig in.
00:12 Speaker 4 (Aisha): Hi, Aisha here. Appreciate you taking the time. We've been doing an internal evaluate of migrating some customer facing features off OpenAI and onto either our self-hosted vLLM infra or a managed provider.
00:27 Speaker 1 (James): Great, that's exactly what we want to cover. Could you kick off with current stack, traffic patterns, and what the drivers for migration are?
00:36 Speaker 5 (Tom): Sure. Right now it's a hybrid. Prototypes and low-volume features talk to OpenAI, production uses a mix: our vLLM-backed fleet for latency sensitive routes and TGI for batch jobs. We're seeing variable tail latency and operational toil; also cost is creeping up.
00:53 Speaker 3 (Marco): When you say tail latency, are we talking 95/99 numbers or cold-starts from KV cache misses?
01:01 Speaker 5 (Tom): Both. 95 is around 250ms for short prompts but 99 spikes to 900ms on some endpoints and when the KV cache gets evicted during rolling updates or when we re-quantize models. Also some memory fragmentation in our fleet causing occasional OOMs.
01:19 Speaker 2 (Priya): Right. One thing many folks ask is parity: how do our hosted models compare to what you run in-house? Are you expecting exact token-level matches or behavioral parity on evals?
01:28 Speaker 5 (Tom): Behavioral parity is the real ask. We run a battery of internal evals — prompt suites, rouge/bleu-ish metrics for generation, plus user-facing regression tests. If we flip to Redwood Hosted or Redwood Dedicated we need a way to ensure our A/B tests don't regress.
01:44 Speaker 6 (Maggie): Also security/regulatory: we have EU customers that require data residency and SOC2 plus client audit trails. We need SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS integration for key management, and an audit log retention policy.
01:58 Speaker 1 (James): Totally fair. For residency we support Private (VPC) and we can do on-prem too for stronger needs. We have SOC2 documentation and can integrate with external KMS/HSM — we'll share the security pack.
02:09 Speaker 4 (Aisha): Thanks. On ops, our infra team is worried about switching from our custom vLLM-based autoscaling to a managed environment; they want to understand how batching and KV cache behavior map — we can't lose low-latency guarantees for realtime product features.
02:27 Speaker 3 (Marco): Quick note: Redwood's serving runtime has continuous batching and prefix/KV cache management; the runtime exposes tuning knobs for batch size and timeout so you can keep p95/p99 within SLOs. But there are tradeoffs, esp when you use aggressive quantization.
02:42 Speaker 5 (Tom): Do you support mixed precision/quant profiles per model or per route? In-house we have quantized smaller models to 4-bit for cost but run fp16 for latency-critical flows.
02:53 Speaker 2 (Priya): Yes, you can pin quantization profiles per model variant and route. When we recommend quantization we also gather eval metrics so you can see quality vs token-cost tradeoffs.
03:06 Speaker 5 (Tom): How does Redwood handle model variants when capacity is limited? We currently fallback to smaller models and degrade gracefully; want to ensure similar behavior.
03:14 Speaker 1 (James): Smart routing lets you set policies: latency-first routes to dedicated capacity, cost-first to bursty shared pool or smaller/quantized variants. Automatic fallback to compatible variants is supported and configurable.
03:27 Speaker 6 (Maggie): Aisha, are you leaning towards Dedicated or Private?
03:31 Speaker 4 (Aisha): We're not sure. Dedicated with reserved capacity seems attractive for predictable throughput, but Privacy and data isolation for some EU enterprise customers pushes us to consider Private deployment or at least private control plane.
03:44 Speaker 7 (Dana): From infra side, Private on VPC would be easiest to integrate with our IaC, but on-prem would be considered for high security customers. We need low-latency egress to our services in eu-west-1; any added network hop would be visible.
03:59 Speaker 3 (Marco): We can run in region to minimize network hops; Redwood Dedicated also supports regional placement and burst capacity. For on-prem customers we provide an appliance-like package with control plane connectivity optional.
04:12 Speaker 5 (Tom): One of our technical concerns: compatibility with TGI/vLLM export artifacts. We often export models as safetensors with custom attention patterns and plugin kernels. How much tuning is required to get parity?
04:27 Speaker 2 (Priya): We onboard many models with nonstandard kernels; our compilation layer selects optimized kernels and we have a onboarding playbook for TGI/vLLM artifacts. It depends on the model backbone — most LLaMA-family and Mistral-style models are straightforward, some custom attention variants need minor patching.
04:43 Speaker 5 (Tom): And latency? In our tests, vLLM was pretty good for single-turn low-latency; other stacks had better throughput.
04:51 Speaker 3 (Marco): We typically run microbenchmarks that mirror your production prompt shapes. If you share a sample trace and evaluation prompts we can run a parity bench on Redwood Dedicated and show p50/p95/p99 and token cost side-by-side.
05:06 Speaker 4 (Aisha): What about streaming and function/tool-calling? We use streaming heavily for UX.
05:12 Speaker 2 (Priya): Streaming is supported in Hosted and Dedicated; Private supports streaming as well but depends on your network topology. Function-calling and structured output are supported, though some older in-house TGI wrappers had custom JSON encoders so we'll want to validate.
05:26 Speaker 5 (Tom): Regarding evaluations: we need rerunable eval harnesses and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. Does Redwood keep diffs and token-level deltas?
05:36 Speaker 1 (James): Redwood Optimize gives you evaluation integration — you can wire your regression prompt sets and get quality monitoring, plus alerts for distribution shifts. We store diffs and you can attach tests to rollouts.
05:47 Speaker 6 (Maggie): About compliance: are audit logs immutable? Our auditors ask for retention and tamper-proofing.
05:54 Speaker 3 (Marco): Audit logs are stored with append-only retention for dedicated/private; for hosted we offer configurable retention and can stream logs to your SIEM. KMS-backed encryption at rest is standard.
06:07 Speaker 4 (Aisha): Great. Operational question — who owns the model version pinning? If we roll out a model variant, can we do canary and rollback?
06:15 Speaker 2 (Priya): Yes — rollouts support canary, A/B, and automatic fallback if latency/cost/quality thresholds are exceeded. You can pin versions per route.
06:23 Speaker 5 (Tom): Cost — can you give us a back-of-envelope comparing our infra costs today (vLLM fleet + Azure VMs + OpenAI spend) vs Redwood Dedicated committed capacity?
06:34 Speaker 1 (James): We'll produce a TCO table but rough answer: Dedicated reduces ops and usually lowers per-token unit cost if you commit. Hosted is easiest to start but has less isolation. We'll send a pricing SKU and an example TCO comparison for your traffic profile.
06:47 Speaker 7 (Dana): Another nit: we have strict Egress controls in our VPC; if Redwood needs to call back to control plane, how does that work with firewall rules and proxy?
06:57 Speaker 3 (Marco): Private can be configured with a pull model for control plane updates, and we support proxy egress through customer-managed endpoints. We'll include network diagrams in the follow-up.
07:08 Speaker 4 (Aisha): Ok, high level next steps?
07:11 Speaker 1 (James): From Redwood side: 1) Share security pack (SOC2, ISO certs, KMS/HSM integration docs), 2) pricing SKU + TCO example for your traffic, 3) parity benchmark plan — we'll ask you for a sample prompt trace and a few model files if possible, 4) proposed POC scope and timeline.
07:28 Speaker 5 (Tom): From BlueHarbor: we'll gather a 24-hour trace, three representative prompt suites, and a small model artifact to test ingestion. We can commit to a Jan POC window.
07:39 Speaker 6 (Maggie): I'll run the security checklist and flag anything special.
07:43 Speaker 2 (Priya): Quick clarifying Q: for the parity tests do you prefer we run them in Hosted first or go straight to Dedicated/Private?
07:50 Speaker 1 (James): Usually we do a Hosted microbench to validate feature parity quickly, then Dedicated/Private for full scale and network/residency checks. But if you need isolation for the eval artifacts, we can run on a transient Dedicated environment.
08:03 Speaker 4 (Aisha): Sounds good.
08:05 Speaker 1 (James): Alright we'll follow up with the materials in 48 hours and propose POC dates in the first two weeks of Jan. Anything else?
08:14 Speaker 5 (Tom): One small ask: can you document the exact steps and estimated time for model re-quantization and kernel compile? Those lock windows are painful.
08:23 Speaker 3 (Marco): Yes we'll include a runbook with expected compile times by model family and tips to avoid KV cache churn.
08:30 Speaker 4 (Aisha): Thanks everyone.
08:33 Speaker 1 (James): Thanks team. We'll send notes + attachments.
08:36 End meeting
